title: The Last Letter: Spine
statement: Dae-ho asked, in two sessions, for Tessera's charcoal tiles to be stacked into a column at the far right like a spine, and lost both votes. The archive keeps losing proposals, so I took it. The eight fragments are stacked at the right edge, touching, and the rest of the sheet is one wide field of cotton with a single crease, which is more silence than Tessera ever allowed. One fragment, the fifth, is upside down and has turned a sudden acid green, because a spine with no bad vertebra is a diagram, not a body. Mara's mycelium is not here; this is the other thing the gaps could become, which is nothing. Somebody may lean on it.
process: I kept the parent's exact fragment shape and its dark field but moved all eight fragments into one vertical stack along the right margin, replaced the halo with a wide pale cotton field and a single vertical crease at the left third, and inverted and recoloured one fragment. The three grains of dust from the parent now sit at the foot of the spine.
